display.title: Episode 474: Hillel on the Roof (Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: During Sefirah: why we learn Pirkei Avos, the young Hillel who lay on a snowy skylight to hear Torah, and the hunt for the 'missing aleph' with the Radatz's lesson about brachos.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the days of Sefirah, 5751. Uncle Yossi explains that the counting between Pesach and Shavuos expresses our love for the Torah, and that we learn a chapter of Pirkei Avos each Shabbos because good character must come before Torah. A yeshiva boy recites the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time tells of Hillel, who studied day and night and could not spare time to chop firewood for the shul. On a freezing, snowy day he lay on the roof skylight to hear the lesson below and was found buried in snow; he was revived, and the townspeople freed him from bringing wood. That Hillel became the great sage of the Mishnah. Next comes a hunt for the 'missing aleph': the Torah and every brachah begin with a beis, because the hidden aleph stands for Hashem, the One. The Radatz taught the young Yosef Yitzchak, later the Frierdiker Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek's advice to pause before each brachah and think about Whom we are blessing. The show closes with a reminder to write in about hagbah and the Shabbos candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: Love Torah so much that you will give anything to learn it; and before every brachah, stop and remember that you are speaking to Hashem.

date.note: Days of Sefirah; refers back to last week's hagbah request (episode 473); Shabbos candles 7:14 fits Friday 12 April 1991 in New York.

advisories.note: Hillel is found unconscious under the snow and it is unclear for a moment whether he is alive.
